headline: Broad-based growth and margin gains; guidance raised
summary_short: Dover reported Q2 2026 revenue of $2,190M, up 6.9% y/y (5% organic), with all five segments posting positive organic growth; GAAP diluted EPS from continuing operations of $2.31 rose 14% and adjusted diluted EPS of $2.74 rose 12%. The company raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS guidance to $10.55-$10.75.
summary_long: Revenue rose 6.9% y/y to $2,190M (5% organic), led by Clean Energy & Fueling (+8.6% organic) and Climate & Sustainability Technologies (+8.3% organic); Pumps & Process Solutions was slowest at +0.4% organic. Segment earnings margin expanded to 24.0% from 23.2% as execution on higher volumes outpaced input-cost inflation. Operating income grew 10.5% to $391.8M and GAAP EPS from continuing operations rose 14% to $2.31; adjusted EPS of $2.74 was up 12%. Free cash flow was $188.4M vs $151.4M a year ago. Bookings of $2,331M outpaced revenue, extending an order-momentum streak. Dover raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $10.55-$10.75 (GAAP EPS $8.94-$9.14), on 6-8% revenue growth (4-6% organic).

drivers.explanation: All five segments delivered positive organic growth; Clean Energy & Fueling (+8.6% organic) and Climate & Sustainability Technologies (+8.3% organic) led, with Pumps & Process Solutions the softest at +0.4% organic. Acquisitions added 1.2ppt and currency 0.9ppt.
Gross profit grew roughly in line with revenue; the release does not break out a specific driver for the gross-margin line separate from segment-level cost execution.

Management said continued operational execution on incremental volumes more than offset input-cost inflation; segment earnings margin rose to 24.0% from 23.2%, and revenue growth (+6.8%) outpaced cost-of-revenue growth (+6.3%).
Net income tracked the operating-income gain; interest expense rose modestly while other income improved, and the provision for income taxes grew slower than pre-tax earnings.
EPS grew faster than net income (13.9% vs 11.9%) because weighted diluted shares outstanding fell 1.8% y/y, consistent with ongoing buyback activity.
Cash grew y/y on higher free cash flow generation ($188.4M this quarter vs $151.4M a year ago); the release does not itemize a specific one-time source for the cash build.

CEO Richard Tobin framed the quarter as broad-based, with bookings outpacing shipments and growing double digits, improving visibility into the second half and supporting the raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance.
